info.name: OCR Flow
info.summary: Make scans and images searchable: OCR in place, nothing left behind
info.description:
OCR Flow finds the files in a Nextcloud folder that carry no text — scans, photos of documents, image-only PDFs — and gives them a searchable text layer without moving or renaming them.
The control plane is this app: it owns the queue, the per-file state and the UI. The actual recognition runs in a companion worker (a plain HTTP client of this app's own OCS endpoints, not an AppAPI/ExApp), so the heavy work — PDF rasterising, cloud OCR calls, font embedding — never blocks a Nextcloud request.
Behaviour worth knowing:
* Nothing is overwritten. An existing `report.pdf` never becomes the target of an image conversion; the app picks `report(1).pdf` the way Nextcloud itself does. * Conversion is reversible. An image becomes a PDF with the original JPEG embedded bit-for-bit, and the worker can hand the original back with its EXIF intact. * Nothing is silently dropped. Nextcloud does not retry failed event deliveries, so the queue is reconciled on a schedule instead of relying on the event alone. * Fail closed. If the classifier cannot decide whether a file is a scan, the job errors and the file is left untouched.
